title: Private and Public
author: Dangerous_Three_8506
selftext:
Does anyone know if there is a way to make the AI realize particular part of the code is Private and it isn't allowed to touch it at all. I am the one that is supposed to edit it, not the AI. I don't want the AI to touch certain parts of my code. I might have to switch to copy and paste with the AI if it can't do this task.

For example, I have a weapon that has finished being reviewed and all its stats are perfect. I would consider it to be a Legacy Item where other weapons are touched by AI with prompts but this weapon cannot be touched. 

The above is just an example of the problem. The real problem I am having is more complex than this where I have a header that is reviewed by AI all the time and I don't want the AI to ever touch some values in the class. It's like private parts of the class are not private anymore. I want AI to tell me it needs a human to proceed with the change.

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body:
I'm using Cursor IDE. I have added a rule "do not touch *.tscn and *.tres. Reading - okay, edditing - never". It never had broke that rule, so it kinda works

Same way you can make global rule "do not touch the items/swords/ folder". If there will be an urgency - it will ask you anyway

Alternatively you could flag the folder as ignored, i think every agentic software let you do so. But then AI will be unable to read it. So i find the "rule" solution more appealing

replies.author: Dangerous_Three_8506
replies.body: Its a class I am working with. The ai needs to touch the public part of the class and never touch the private. If it touches the private I freak out because all my math and collision knowledge changes and I have to review everything.

replies.author: StretchedNut
replies.body: Do you not have version control that shows you differences and previous versions?

replies.author: unfamily_friendly
replies.body: Add the rule "Obey the comments, started with [AI], unconditionally", and then add a comment "[AI] Do not edit this function!" to your methods

replies.author: ipreuss
replies.body: You should have automated tests that fail when it happens.

comments.author: spinglass_dev
comments.body:
Just throw it in your AGENTS.md

Be aware that models (esp. older ones) can be a bit "forgetful" about the rules in there, especially when the context window gets full. But in general that should fix it for you 95% of the time.

replies.author: Dangerous_Three_8506
replies.body:
What are MD files before AI? I have so many questions as I work. The frontier of AI is so fun.

What were MD files used for before AI? Now with AI how have they changed. These are my questions all the time.

Headers are not the same anymore. The private and public classes are not real to me. The ai touching private pisses me off.

replies.author: spinglass_dev
replies.body:
.md is the extension for "Markdown". Markdown is just an extremely simple format for writing text, like .txt or .doc.   
  
It's basically just text...it also allows for some very basic quality of life stuff like sections, titles, italics, and horizontal line breaks. The file size is a lot smaller for storage and more universally readable than something like Microsoft Word. 

Before AI, devs used .md files a lot for writing documentation like README files (meant for other humans to read). After AI, they are used even more because it's a very friendly format for AIs to read and write. 

\>The private and public classes are not real to me. The ai touching private pisses me off.

That's not what the "private" in "private class" means. 

I recommend asking the AI a lot of questions as you go. It will help avoid frustrations from misunderstandings.

comments.author: LazyAp3
comments.body: Thats what an agent is for and then you test run it

replies.author: Dangerous_Three_8506
replies.body: Im still learning. What is an agent to you? Thanks for your help.

comments.author: EnvironmentFirst4839
comments.body: All tuning numbers should be data… separate your data from the logic itself into its own data folder/taxonomy. Create a dev panel in game that allows you to adjust any or all values with sliders/inputs/locks/etc. Ask Claude to help you set up your project in a way where AI can’t and won’t change your .tres files outside of adding the feasible range of values on each when first created.

comments.author: -Star-Walker-
comments.body: Ehmm … should not happen at all in a solid well architected code. That’s the part you should have planned before you started writing any code. Software architecture is essential!

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body:
Put all of this into your 'AGENTS.md 'file, telling the agent which pieces/folders/files/documents are off limits, then ensure before each and every pass your agent reads the 'AGENTS.md' file (it it supposed to, do not trust that it will). This will prevent most of it. 

Have the agent 1) read 'AGENTS.md', **2)** execute the instructions you have provided (I put mine into markdowns and execute against them for historical documentation and clarity), **3)** Write a full report of what he has done and stick it in the docs folder (*because you should have one of these for sure*), **4)** have the agent summarize his work in 'changes.md' (*because you should also have one of these*), **5)** offer one of these options *a:* wait for manual review (*you look at it make sure he didn't fuck it up and then commit it yourself*), *b:* commit the work and wait for manual review (*let him commit the work and hope he didn't fuck it up*), *c:* continue with the next phase (*assuming you are running a phased automation type plan*). 

Ensure you use git, and commit after every work phase, the nif the agent DOES go outside it's scope it's very simple to see what it did and  revert the changes. 

Be well, keep creating. Good luck.
